title: Daily ingest, case list and reconciliation triggers, hand-offs and workflow IDs
ruling: AceIngestCheck (type per Arch v5) on rwb-source-data, ID ace-ingest-check-{businessDate}, started by POST /v1/business-days/{date}/ready, by Schedule rwb-source-data-ace-late-check at 05:30 Asia/Bangkok (SKIP, 1 h catch-up) or by the flagged Control-M poll; conflict policy USE_EXISTING, reuse policy ALLOW_DUPLICATE; polls v_ace_batch_status every 5 min and closes when every due source is COMPLETED or after 24 h. ReconciliationWorkflow, ID recon-{businessDate}, is a child of CaseListBuildWorkflow, started after case_list_row commits. rwb-source-data consumes none of its own topics; CDC-02650 and CDC-02790 are rejected.

title: Freshness stamp state model
ruling: Keep the data_product_load key (product_code, business_date); only RWB-P1-E1015-APP writes the table. Expected business date: the latest bank business day before the run date (v_ace_holiday, DP14); weekly products by cycle day. On time if and only if completed_at < expected_by (Asia/Bangkok, to the second). A row is inserted LOADED only when every mapped source is COMPLETED for the date: source_system = the last source to complete, source_extracted_at = earliest started_at, loaded_at = latest completed_at. The stamp in use is the row with the greatest business_date. At expected_by with no LOADED row, or on FAILED, the stamp in use is set STALE with stale_flagged_at and MSG-P1-001, and no second AceDataLate is published. Never-stamped: FreshnessQuery answers businessDate null, status STALE. A late batch inserts a new LOADED row and the earlier row stays STALE. A restatement adds 1 to duplicate_count, publishes no event and raises an alert. COMPLETED then FAILED: STALE, and AceDataLate once. An older date arriving after a newer one is kept as history, with no AceDataReady. E1055 counts its repeats in its own metric; the E1069 writer clause is removed.

title: Reconciliation tolerance (DL25)
ruling: DL25 option A (the Decision Log v12 recommendation): one parameter, recon.tolerance.pct = 0.00 percent, version 1, held in the rwb-case parameter catalog and read through RWB-P3-E1042-CON; recon.caselist.tolerance.pct is retired. PASS when the absolute variance percent is at most the tolerance (inclusive), so any difference is BREAK: publish HELD and MSG-P1-012. There is no NOT_RUN value (LOV-REC-RESULT holds PASS and BREAK): a run that cannot proceed writes no row and the run is FAILED. A clean day is one where every REC-01 and REC-02 result is PASS under version 1 and no new REC-05 orphan appears. Unblocks build: yes. DL25 moves to Decisions taken, for Data lead confirmation.

title: Section B views dependency (DL43)
ruling: DL43 recommended answer (Decision Log v12): yes, scope and dates as in RWB-ACE-001; build to it. All Section B code is built and tested in DEV and the pipeline against the RWB-P1-E1065-CON Tier 2 DDL fixture (ACE schema, then V0001, then Section A, then Section B). In SIT, UAT and PROD the Section B migration waits for the ACE dependency gate, and the features deploy with their flags off. With the flag off: POST ready answers 202, no stamp is written and no AceDataReady or AceDataLate is published, and the status answer is LATE; the DailyCaseList Schedule is paused; FreshnessQuery answers STALE with a null date; Section B alert rules are not armed, and the health check reports the flag state. If DL43 is answered B, the fallback scope in Decision Log v12 applies and a new RD-P1 entry re-plans it. Unblocks build: yes; switching the features on waits for RWB-ACE-001.

title: Rollback standard with forward-only migrations
ruling: Order: switch the flag off first; if the flag does not cover the fault, redeploy the previous image tag and chart of rwb-source-data (the release note names the capabilities this reverts). Never reverse a migration: fix forward with a new V<next> on the rwb_source_data sequence; there is no U*.sql and no down script. Migrations are expand-only and work with the previous tag; drops and renames come only after the flag is removed; the previous tag's smoke test runs against the migrated schema (the rollback AC). Worker Versioning keeps the previous build ID; no workflow is terminated; consumer offsets are not reset; Schedules added by the release are paused. First release: flag off, worker scaled to zero, Schedules paused. The DB state set is Pending, Applied and Failed ('undone' removed); a seed fails on an existing key; ACE001 tables change only through ACE-team forward migrations. Rollback is triggered by failed post-deploy checks, no JOB-22 smoke result, or an incident attributed to the release.

title: Retention run interface between P5 and P1, and the held-cases read from P3
ruling: P1 publishes POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/retention-runs: Idempotency-Key {runDate}:{ruleVersion}; body ruleVersion, runDate and rules[] (productCode, tableName, recordClass, retentionMonths, ageBasis, endAction ARCHIVE or REVIEW). It answers 202 with runId; 409 when a run for the run date is active; 422 for refused rules or a replayed key. GET /retention-runs/{runId} answers the status and the counts per table. The fake covers success, 409, 422, timeout and 5xx. RetentionRunWorkflow ID: retention-run-{runDate}. P5's RetentionRunWorkflow passes its P1 rows, calls in one hop (2 s) and polls every 5 min; /admin/retention-archive is withdrawn. P3 publishes, in RWB-P3-E1021-CON and rwb-case.yaml, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/retention-exclusions (held or open cases with caseId, caseNumber, reason, accountKeys and personKeys; paged) and GET /cases/closure-dates?closedBefore= (closedAt with the keys). These replace CaseHoldQuery. An unreadable answer fails the run before selection.
